# PR #2871: Patch: the logo stays sharp on Safari and iPhone

Closes #2845

## What changed and why

WebKit rasterizes everything an SVG filter touches at 1x and upscales the bitmap, so the `feDropShadow` filters on the logo (`shadow` on each card, `lift` on the J, the star and the wordmark) made the whole JackiOh mark soft on 3x iPhone screens, while Chromium renders the same files sharp.

- `apps/web/scripts/brand-logo.py`: deleted the `shadow` and `lift` filters from `DEFS`; shadows are now drawn as pure vector stacked strokes via new `shaded()` / `j_and_star()` helpers (each shadow is the same shape again, offset by `dy`, in 6 layers of widening stroke at a share of the opacity; geometry written once in `<defs>` and `<use>`d). Same shadow color, offset, width and opacity as before. The `-wood` variants keep their `grainDark`/`grainLight`/`logoGlow` filters (no screen shows them).
- `apps/web/README.md`: logo paragraph notes the stacked-strokes shadows.
- Regenerated the 8 SVGs in `apps/web/public/brand` and 10 PNGs in `photos/logo` with the script (applied as `git cherry-pick -n 70cf8af9`, 20 files, nothing else).
- New `apps/web/src/skeleton/brand-sharp.test.ts`: fails if any brand SVG other than the two `-wood` ones contains `<filter` or `filter=` (title cites `#2845`, no `R…` token).

## How I tested it

- Script idempotence: `sha256sum` over all brand SVGs and PNGs before and after rerunning `python3 apps/web/scripts/brand-logo.py` — identical (rerun is a no-op; SVG bytes equal the cherry-pick exactly).
- Pre-fix failure: every pre-fix non-wood SVG contains `<filter` and `filter=` (2 and 1–3 occurrences), so the new test fails on the base tree by construction; now `grep -l 'filter' apps/web/public/brand/*.svg` prints only the two `-wood` files.
- Before/after renders of `jackioh-mark.svg` and `jackioh-logo-stacked.svg` in Chromium at `deviceScaleFactor: 2` (`/tmp/cmp-mark-before/after.png`, `/tmp/cmp-stacked-before/after.png`): ink bounding boxes match within ~6px at 1x, shadow ink is present in the after images (7.9%/6.0% of pixels darken the page background), and pixels with visible change are confined to the artwork edges (9.5%/5.9%) — same placement and shadows, sharper edges. I have no image viewer in this environment, so the comparison is quantitative (own stdlib PNG decoder); a person should eyeball the four PNGs.

- WebKit check: no WebKit renderer exists on this machine (`~/.cache/ms-playwright` holds only Chromium) — **a person needs to verify the J is sharp on an iPhone.**

- The repo has no Playwright npm package, so the script's raster step ran via a throwaway `playwright-core` install plus a small `require("playwright")` shim in `/tmp` pointing at the cached Chromium 1247 (resolved through `NODE_PATH`); no repo files were touched for this.
- `pip install --break-system-packages` was needed for `fonttools`/`brotli` (PEP 668 system Python).
- The WASM build took ~50 minutes under contention with other agents' builds on this shared machine; no code changes were needed for it.

No ruling was created or cited (brand artwork is not spec-governed), and the CSS halos in `skeleton.css` and `tavern.css` were left alone as instructed.

````text
# #2845: Patch: the logo stays sharp on Safari and iPhone
Opened by @MaxGoetzmann.

### What happens

On an iPhone (Safari/WebKit, 3x screen), the JackiOh mark over the menus' skeletons (`src/skeleton/skeleton.css:53`, R2115000) is visibly fuzzy next to the sharp text around it, for example on Statistics → Game figures while it loads. The full-screen loading panel is worse: it draws the bigger stacked logo (`ShellPanel` in `src/main.tsx`, `SHELL_LOGO` = `/brand/jackioh-logo-stacked.svg`).

### Root cause

These files are already vectors (`apps/web/public/brand/*.svg`, drawn by `apps/web/scripts/brand-logo.py`), so the file format isn't the problem. The problem is the SVG **filters** inside them. Every shadow in the logo is an `feDropShadow` filter:

- `filter="url(#shadow)"` on each card's whole `<g>` (`card()`), and
- `filter="url(#lift)"` on the J, the star (`front_card()`, `card_back_art()`) and the wordmark (`wordmark()`).

WebKit renders the content an SVG filter applies to at 1x and then scales that bitmap up. So on a retina phone the whole of each card, the J, the star and the wordmark come out soft, not just their shadows. Chromium renders the same files sharp at 2x, which is why it doesn't show on desktop Chrome.

Confidence: high, but proven only by elimination. The same files render sharp in Chromium at deviceScaleFactor 2; only the filters differ between what is sharp and what is soft in the screenshot; and the 1x rendering of SVG filters is a known WebKit behavior. It has not been reproduced in a WebKit renderer (none was available in the session that found it).

Secondary suspects, if the mark is still soft after the fix: the CSS `filter: drop-shadow(...)` halos on the skeleton's `::before` (`skeleton.css:55`) and on `.shell-panel__logo` (`src/auth/tavern.css:655`). Leave them unless the check below shows they also blur.

### What should happen

The mark, the stacked logo, the horizontal logo, the card-back art (the Jlorious card back, `src/cards/cosmetics.css`), the small mark and the app icon stay as sharp as the text on a 3x WebKit screen. They should look the same as now, shadows included.

### The fix

In `apps/web/scripts/brand-logo.py`, draw each shadow without a filter: the shape again, offset by `dy`, several times, each layer a wider stroke at a share of the opacity, so the layers add up to the old opacity under the shape and fade out about 2×`stdDeviation` past its edge. Write the geometry once in `<defs>` and `<use>` it, so the wordmark's long path isn't copied six times. Then remove the `shadow` and `lift` filters from `DEFS`, rerun the script (`pip install fonttools brotli`; it rasterizes with Playwright's Chromium) and commit the 8 SVGs and 10 PNGs it rewrites.

The `-wood` variants keep their `grainDark`/`grainLight`/`logoGlow` filters: no screen shows them (only `photos/logo` PNGs are made from them).

**A working candidate already exists:** commit `70cf8af9` on branch `fix/logo-crisp-on-webkit` (20 files, script + regenerated SVGs/PNGs + a line in `apps/web/README.md`). Cherry-pick it or redo it, then add the test below. The unmodified script reproduces the committed files byte for byte, so the diff from main is only the shadow change.

### Acceptance

- [ ] A vitest in `apps/web` (next to `src/skeleton/Skeleton.test.tsx` / `src/routes/gate.test.tsx`, which already read these files) fails if any SVG in `public/brand` other than the two `-wood` ones contains `<filter` or `filter=`, and names this issue.
- [ ] `public/brand/*.svg` and `photos/logo/*.png` are regenerated by the script, not edited by hand; rerunning it changes nothing.
- [ ] Before/after renders of `jackioh-mark.svg` and `jackioh-logo-stacked.svg` in Chromium look the same (shadows present, same placement), attached to the PR.
- [ ] If a WebKit renderer is available (Playwright `webkit`, `deviceScaleFactor: 3`), a before/after crop showing the J sharp; otherwise say in the PR that a person checks it on an iPhone.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web test` and `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` green.

### How to reproduce

1. On an iPhone, open any menu screen that shows a skeleton (e.g. Statistics) on a slow connection, or the full-screen loading panel.
2. Compare the J and the card edges with the text: the logo is soft.
3. Desktop Chrome on the same page: sharp.

### Where

The client (menus and loading screens), `apps/web/scripts/brand-logo.py` and `apps/web/public/brand`.

### Version or commit

`main` at `6b6cbcb0`; the logo landed in #2747.

`apps/web/src/skeleton/brand-sharp.test.ts` (new file):

```ts
import { readdirSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { dirname, join } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

const BRAND = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..", "..", "public", "brand");

// #2845: WebKit rasterizes whatever an SVG filter touches at 1x and scales it up, so an
// feDropShadow blurred the whole logo on a phone. The wood variants keep their grain and
// glow filters (no screen shows them); every other brand SVG must be filter-free.
describe("#2845 the brand stays sharp on WebKit", () => {
  it("#2845 no shipped brand SVG but the two -wood ones uses an SVG filter", () => {
    const files = readdirSync(BRAND).filter((f) => f.endsWith(".svg"));
    for (const name of [
      "jackioh-card-back.svg",
      "jackioh-icon.svg",
      "jackioh-logo-stacked.svg",
      "jackioh-logo.svg",
      "jackioh-mark-small.svg",
      "jackioh-mark.svg",
    ]) {
      expect(files).toContain(name);
    }
    expect(files.filter((f) => f.endsWith("-wood.svg")).sort()).toEqual([
      "jackioh-logo-wood.svg",
      "jackioh-mark-wood.svg",
    ]);
    for (const file of files) {
      if (file.endsWith("-wood.svg")) continue;
      const text = readFileSync(join(BRAND, file), "utf8");
      expect(text, file).not.toContain("<filter");
      expect(text, file).not.toContain("filter=");
    }
  });
});
```

Run `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/skeleton/brand-sharp.test.ts`, then the two existing readers `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/skeleton/Skeleton.test.tsx` and `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/routes/gate.test.tsx`, then `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`. All green.

- [ ] Before/after Chromium renders of the mark and stacked logo look the same (shadows present, same placement) and are attached to the PR; the PR text says whether a WebKit crop exists or a person checks on an iPhone.
- [ ] Web typecheck and the three vitest files above are green.

- PNG bytes depend on the local Chromium build, so they may differ from the candidate commit's PNGs; the guarantee is rerun-idempotence on this machine, not byte-equality with that commit. SVG bytes are pure Python plus the repo-pinned Alegreya and must match exactly.
- The `<defs><… id="s<N>"/></defs>` ids come from a module-level counter consumed in `main()`'s fixed call order; reordering calls or resetting the counter renumbers every id and dirties all SVGs, so keep the order and the counter as cherry-picked.
- `photos/logo/preview-*.png` are not written by the script and must stay untouched, or the diff gains files the rerun cannot reproduce.

## Open questions

- No WebKit renderer was available where the issue was found; if none is on this machine either, only a person with an iPhone can confirm the J is sharp, which the PR text must say. The builder changes nothing else on that account.

import { readdirSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { dirname, join } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

const BRAND = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..", "..", "public", "brand");

// #2845: WebKit rasterizes whatever an SVG filter touches at 1x and scales it up, so an
// feDropShadow blurred the whole logo on a phone. The wood variants keep their grain and
// glow filters (no screen shows them); every other brand SVG must be filter-free.

      "jackioh-icon.svg",
      "jackioh-logo-stacked.svg",
      "jackioh-logo.svg",

});
